newsitem.title: UK: Pharmacia confirms Q1 profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia confirms Q1 profit fall.

text.p: Troubled Swedish-U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc on Tuesday confirmed a fall in first-quarter profits and sales, and set out plans to turn the newly-merged company's fortunes around.
The group, which issued its third profit warning in six months last week, said earnings per share before exceptional items dropped 16 percent to $0.37, while sales fell 6.1 percent to $1.635 billion.

The company said five percentage points of the drop in sales was due to currencies, particularly the strengthening of the dollar against the yen. It set out changes to its currency hedging policy, including extending the hedging period.

Board chairman Richard Brown said: "We are disappointed with our performance. We will improve it. Our board places top priority on taking all necessary measures to restore confidence, and is committed to delivering long-term shareholder value."
The company outlined a number of measures to "significantly improve short-and long-term results," including investment in new products and focusing on the core pharmaceuticals operations.

Pharmacia & Upjohn said the search for a new chief executive to replace John Zabriskie, who departed unexpectedly last January, was at "an advanced stage," with an announcement expected "in the near future."
